bull.b: Completion of dosing advances CDI-988 from enrollment into the data-generation phase, creating a meaningful clinical milestone. Earlier human testing showed favorable safety and tolerability, while the current study evaluates prevention and treatment efficacy in a defined norovirus challenge model.

A structure-based design approach gives Cocrystal a coherent scientific foundation for generating antiviral candidates across multiple pathogens. Its focus on viral replication and programs spanning influenza, coronaviruses, norovirus and hepatitis C creates opportunities to reuse expertise across a broader pipeline.

The $5 million placement improves Cocrystal’s capital position while it advances its antiviral programs, and participation by longtime investor OPKO provides strategic support. The financing helps sustain clinical execution and signals continued backing for the company’s platform.

bear.b: Cocrystal continues to consume substantial cash because operating activities do not yet generate funding. Although burn has improved from 2024, persistently negative free cash flow means clinical development depends on outside financing or other non-operating sources over the coming periods.

Higher leverage combined with a sharply smaller asset base leaves Cocrystal with a thinner financial buffer. Debt exceeding equity can reduce flexibility during continued development spending, increase dependence on capital markets, and make funding setbacks more consequential.

Revenue remains very small relative to the company’s operating expenses, and substantial net and operating losses show that Cocrystal has not established a durable commercial earnings base. Its cost structure is still oriented toward R&D and development rather than scalable product revenue.
